issue: `parseQuery()` in qs.mjs doesn't decode values: parseQuery('q=hello%20world') should give { q: 'hello world' }, and '+' also means a space. A key that appears more than once becomes an array of its values in order ('t=a&t=b' -> { t: ['a', 'b'] }). A leading '?' is ignored.
prompt_template:
Bug report for the project in {workdir}:

`parseQuery()` in qs.mjs doesn't decode values: parseQuery('q=hello%20world') should give { q: 'hello world' }, and '+' also means a space. A key that appears more than once becomes an array of its values in order ('t=a&t=b' -> { t: ['a', 'b'] }). A leading '?' is ignored.

Fix the bug in the source code (not the tests). Run the tests with `node --test`. When you're done, reply with a short summary of what you changed and whether the tests pass.
